NODES

A minimal model: honest nodes report the true value 100 plus small noise; corrupt nodes collude on a false number; the network takes the median. Real networks add many data sources, staking, reputation and signatures, so this is not any protocol’s actual parameter set.

[SHEET 00.E] · FALSIFICATION

What would prove this wrong

Proposition 4: institutions and autonomous agents move to verifiable settlement rails. Confidence in the revised model: 72%, the lowest of its four, so the washes on this sheet are drawn at the 70–84% density.

  • Institutions wind down public-chain products, or tokenized Treasuries and deposits fail to exceed $25B by 2028.
  • G7 regulators prohibit institutional use, or courts refuse to recognize on-chain state as property.
  • An oracle or consensus failure compromises more than $10B of institutional collateral.
  • Autonomous AI agents choose card and bank-API rails over on-chain ones.
[SHEET 00.F] · LIMIT

Truth in, truth out

Verification secures the path, not the source. An oracle network can faithfully deliver a number that was wrong at the origin. The evidence here is reported by vendors and aggregators, adoption is not the same as trust, and the thesis itself stays open: the scale above shows your own files disagree on the threshold.
